summary: Source-anchored research for Editorial commentary in neutral prose. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Wikipedia's guide itself cautions that signs of AI writing are not proof: LLMs are trained on human writing, and such phrasing appears in editorials and blogs, so treat markers as weak evidence. (low confidence)

Wikipedia's NPOV policy instructs editors 'Do not editorialize' and to attribute opinions to reliable sources rather than state them as fact, while uncontested facts are stated directly in the encyclopedia's voice. (high confidence)

Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing says LLM text inflates significance with stock phrases (stands as, testament to, pivotal role, underscores, reflects broader trends), regressing to generic positive language instead of specific facts, so output is less specific and more exaggerated. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Wikipedia's Words to watch lists editorializing markers: notably, it should be noted, arguably, interestingly, essentially, clearly, of course, without a doubt, fortunately, unfortunately. Highlighting something as significant needs attribution. (high confidence)
Connectives such as but, despite, however, although, furthermore can create unsupported relationships between statements, implying an editorial judgement on how facts relate. (medium confidence)

Lexical overrepresentation of LLM-associated words (21 focal words such as delve, intricate, underscore in scientific abstracts) is documented; the study finds model architecture, algorithm and training data do not explain it and RLHF is consistent with playing a role, with ambiguous experimental support. (medium confidence)
